title: Inspiring teens
grammar: Past simple and present perfect for telling life stories and achievements

vocab.example: She is an inspiring young activist.
The teenage entrepreneur started her own company.
Winning the prize was a huge achievement.
Athletes can be role models for young people.
Together, we are stronger — that is solidarity.
Her project had a real impact on the community.

student.repte: We often hear about inspiring teenage entrepreneurs and their successful stories but, who of you will be able to find the most amazing?

products.desc: In small groups, research an inspiring young person and share their story and impact as a video, podcast, digital poster or speech.
Present to the class and take questions from your classmates about the person your group chose.

teacher.repte: The opening Learning Scenario of the year, following the introductory session and the diagnostic test. Students discover the accomplishments of inspiring teens and young adults, and see how much more people achieve with a sense of solidarity — the “Together, we are stronger!” slogan.
teacher.competencies: Llengua Estrangera 2, 7 and 8; Ciutadana CC1; Emprenedora CE1; CPSAA 3; Digital CD2.
teacher.methodology: Project-Based Learning, collaborative learning with peer review, digital literacy for multimodal presentations, student-centred choice of topic.
teacher.assessment: Interpretation of oral and multimodal texts, audience engagement and creativity of the presentation, reliability of the sources used.

title: Art through words
grammar: Descriptive adjectives and relative clauses for profiling an artist

vocab.example: Her artwork is displayed in a small gallery.
We wrote a listicle about the artist's life.
Creativity is at the heart of this project.
The exhibition opens next week.
Persistence helped her become a professional artist.

student.repte: Art is not just old paintings in a museum. Create the profile of a female artist who deserves to be better known — research her life and her work, and present her to the class as a team.

products.desc: A multimedia presentation about a not-so-famous female artist, built in Google Slides, Canva, Genial·ly or a similar tool.
A written listicle covering several aspects of the artist, following the structure of the model provided.
Deliver the presentation in class, ready to ask and answer questions and facilitate the discussion.

teacher.repte: Students find out about young people who applied their creativity and initiative to produce art of various kinds, discovering that art is a living, vibrant form of expression. The group work develops suggesting ideas, listening respectfully, dividing tasks equally and giving constructive feedback.
teacher.competencies: Llengua Estrangera 3, 5 and 6; Ciutadana CC1; Emprenedora CE3; CPSAA 4; Digital CD3.
teacher.methodology: Project-Based Learning in mixed-ability groups, online research, peer review, digital creation tools.
teacher.assessment: Quality of the research and selection of information, structure of the listicle, collaboration and shared credit within the team.

title: The state of our planet
grammar: Present simple and continuous, quantifiers, the passive voice and the first conditional

vocab.example: Air pollution is a serious problem in big cities.
Climate change affects the whole planet.
We produce too much plastic waste.
Recycling helps reduce landfill.
Sustainability means thinking about the future.
Greenhouse gases trap heat in the atmosphere.

student.repte: What are the biggest threats facing our planet? Research them, then design a campaign that persuades your classmates to actually do something about it.

products.desc: Research the global and local threats facing Earth and present a persuasive campaign with interactive elements.
Track what you Know, Want to know and have Learned, and record the sources you used and why they are reliable.
Complete feedback forms for the other campaigns, focusing on strengths and areas for improvement.

teacher.repte: Students analyse global and local environmental problems, evaluate the reliability of their sources, and develop a creative environmental campaign proposal cooperatively.
teacher.competencies: Llengua Estrangera 1, 4 and 9; Ciutadana CC3; Emprenedora CE1; CPSAA 4; Digital CD2.
teacher.methodology: Project-Based Learning, mind-mapping and KWL charts, source-reliability work, cooperative campaign design, digital poster and video tools.
teacher.assessment: Reliability and variety of sources, persuasive use of modals and the first conditional, ability to separate main from secondary ideas.

title: A holiday on the Moon
grammar: Future forms, comparatives and superlatives, and the second conditional

vocab.example: The Moon is an unusual holiday destination.
The accommodation includes a low-gravity room.
The launch is scheduled for next spring.
The hotel is in orbit around the Moon.
You need a spacesuit to walk outside.
Design your trip with an unlimited budget.

student.repte: Imagine you were given the opportunity to design your future holiday in outer space with an unlimited budget. Have you got what it takes to design a travel brochure, website page or promotional video for a Moon holiday package and present it to the class?

products.desc: In teams, plan a Moon holiday — travel logistics, accommodation, activities and challenges — and produce a brochure, web page or promotional video.
Write an email to a host family, applying the register and structure practised in class.
Deliver the advertisement to the class, including the interactive elements, and field questions afterwards.

teacher.repte: Halfway through the year, students take a look at the future. Combining future thinking with holidays, they reflect on how leisure might change, weigh the ethical, social and environmental impacts of space tourism, and learn to appreciate the world as it is now.
teacher.competencies: Llengua Estrangera 2, 5 and 10; Ciutadana CC1; Emprenedora CE3; CPSAA 2; Digital CD5.
teacher.methodology: Project-Based Learning, shared Padlet for vocabulary, KWL charts, source evaluation, differentiated output (brochure, website or video).
teacher.assessment: Persuasive use of comparatives, superlatives and the second conditional, coherence of the travel plan, quality of the multimedia product.

title: School days
grammar: Modals of obligation and prohibition, the passive voice and the second conditional

vocab.example: Our timetable changes every term.
The school has excellent sports facilities.
Students there have to wear a uniform.
School rules are not the same in every country.
Students should have responsibilities too.

student.repte: If you could design your ideal school, what would it look like? What rules would you implement? Uniform or free expression? What would the students' responsibilities be — if any?

products.desc: A collaborative digital leaflet advertising the school your class designs, with its special features, its rules and the students' responsibilities.
Write a for-and-against essay about rules at school, following the structure of the model provided.
Act out a conversation about a personal anecdote at school, paying particular attention to pronunciation and accent.

teacher.repte: The academic world opens the last term. Students learn about the difficult journeys some children make to reach school, give their opinion on the controversial topic of school uniforms, and consider the purpose of school rules and collective decision-making.
teacher.competencies: Llengua Estrangera 3, 5 and 7; Ciutadana CC1; Emprenedora CE3; CPSAA 4; Digital CD1.
teacher.methodology: Project-Based Learning, group decision-making through presenting, suggesting, evaluating and voting, comparative study of education systems.
teacher.assessment: Accuracy of modals of obligation and the second conditional, balance and structure of the for-and-against essay, participation in collective decisions.

title: Thinking outside the box
grammar: The passive voice for describing inventions and the second conditional for hypotheses

vocab.example: The printing press was a life-changing invention.
The inventor never gave up on her idea.
Resilience matters when your first design fails.
They came up with an innovative solution.
Problem-solving is the heart of this project.

student.repte: If you had all the necessary resources, what contribution would you make to human evolution? Will you be innovative enough to create something that makes our life easier or better?

products.desc: In groups, choose a real problem — at school, in town or global — brainstorm solutions, then design an invention and present its design, materials and how it works.
Record how your group took turns, expressed agreement and disagreement, and assigned tasks to reach a joint decision.

teacher.repte: The last stop of the year. Students learn about life-changing inventions and the inventors whose creativity, persistence and resilience produced them, then experience the satisfaction of contributing to society with their own creativity.
teacher.competencies: Llengua Estrangera 2, 3 and 4; Ciutadana CC1; Emprenedora CE3; CPSAA 4; Digital CD1.
teacher.methodology: Collaborative project work, brainstorming and negotiation, conversational strategies for turn-taking and agreement, digital tools for shaping ideas.
teacher.assessment: Fluency and self-confidence while speaking, comprehension of written texts about the origins of an invention, quality of group negotiation.
